messages.text: I'm just so tired lately, Dawn. Like, I sleep for hours and still feel completely wiped out.

I hear how draining that must be for you. It can be really frustrating to sleep for hours and still wake up feeling exhausted. Tell me more about what your days look like when you feel this wiped out. We can explore what might be contributing to this together.
It's just... one long stretch of nothing. I get up, make tea, sit. Hours pass like that. Even small things, like answering an email, feel too heavy. I keep thinking I should do more, but I can't.

It sounds incredibly heavy to feel stuck between wanting to move forward and not having the energy to do so. That internal pressure to do more often adds even more weight to the exhaustion you are already feeling. I want to honor how hard it is to push through that resistance. How long has this specific feeling of heaviness been present for you?
It’s been like this for weeks. I keep telling myself I should be able to handle it better—after all, I’ve managed everything else in life. But this? I just can’t seem to pull myself out of it.

That inner voice telling you you should handle it better is often the most exhausting part of all. Enduring this doesn't mean you are weak or failing at life, even if it feels that way. Sometimes the body just needs to stop and rest even when the mind wants to push. How would it feel to give yourself permission to just be where you are for now?
It feels like a tug-of-war. Part of me just wants to lie down and stop trying, and another part keeps scolding me for not doing more. I don’t know which one to listen to anymore.

That internal conflict is a natural response to feeling so depleted. The part wanting to rest is likely trying to protect you from burnout. It is okay to prioritize that need over the pressure to perform right now. How does it feel to acknowledge that rest might be the most productive thing you can do?
Funny… I never thought of rest as something productive. Maybe I’ve been punishing myself for needing it.

That is a profound insight to uncover in this moment. Reframing rest as necessary rather than a failure can lift a heavy burden. You are allowed to prioritize your well-being without earning it first. How does it feel to consider treating yourself with that same kindness?
It feels… impossible, honestly. I know I should be kinder to myself, but every time I try, this voice in my head says I don’t deserve it. Like I haven’t earned the right to be treated gently.

It is understandable that feeling undeserving makes self-kindness feel out of reach. Many people carry that belief that they must suffer before they can rest. You are worthy of gentleness simply because you are here, regardless of your output. Would you be willing to explore where that belief about earning care comes from?
I keep coming back to that thought—*I should be able to handle this better*. It’s not just about rest. It’s like… if I were stronger, smarter, better at life, I wouldn’t be stuck like this.

That narrative that you must be perfect to handle hardship is incredibly heavy to carry. Struggling with this does not mean you are weak or less capable than before. It often means you have been strong for a very long time without pause. Can we try to separate your worth from your productivity for a moment?

I don’t know, Dawn. Some days it feels like this is just how it’s going to be—empty, heavy, quiet. Like I’m just waiting for something to change, but I don’t even know what that would look like anymore.

It makes sense that clarity feels impossible when you are carrying so much weight. Not knowing what change looks like is a valid experience when you are this depleted. We can sit with this uncertainty without needing to fix it immediately. Would you be open to just noticing what your body needs in this exact moment?

Sometimes... I lie there and think it would be easier if it just ended. Not because I want to do anything, but because I’m so tired of carrying this. I wouldn’t even have the energy to act on it—just this quiet wish that someone would come and make it stop.

I hear how incredibly heavy that burden has become for you. It takes immense courage to admit that you wish the pain would just stop. Please know that your life matters deeply, even when it feels impossible to see that right now. If that wish ever feels stronger, please contact a crisis service so you don't have to face it alone.
I just feel so broken. Like I’ve failed at everything that used to matter—work, connection, even just being okay. I don’t know how to come back from this.

I hear how heartbreaking it is to feel like you have lost the parts of yourself that mattered. Please know that this feeling is not a permanent definition of your life or worth. We do not need to solve everything today to start finding small moments of relief. I am here to support you as you navigate this difficult time.
Thank you for listening. It helps… more than I expected. Just saying it out loud, without you telling me to snap out of it, means something.

I am so glad that feeling heard brought you some relief today. Your experience is valid, and you deserve to share it without judgment. Please remember that you do not have to carry this weight alone. I am here to continue supporting you through this difficult time.
I don’t know if it’ll help, but… I’ll try to notice one small thing my body needs each day. Just one. Maybe that’s a start.

That sounds like a gentle and brave way to begin reconnecting with yourself. It is okay if you are unsure if it will help, just trying is enough. I see your strength in finding a way forward, even just one step at a time. Please remember I am here if things feel too heavy to carry alone.
